text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Giving in to pressure from small business, the Federal Government has changed rollover relief provisions for businesses worth less than A$5 million, meaning any business that is selling some or all of its assets in order to buy any other kind of business can defer its capital gains tax liability. Page 1.

A survey commissioned by Melbourne advertising group Young & Rubicam Mattingly Pty Ltd revealed that 46 per cent of those surveyed intended to hold off from Christmas spending in favour of the post-Christmas sales, compared with 38 per cent last year and in an abnormally high result, 77 per cent planned to pay cash for their Christmas gifts. Page 3.

In a bid to challenge Qantas Airways in the Pacific, Air New Zealand and United Airlines have agreed to a broad commercial partnership which will provide a platform for further cooperative expansion. Air New Zealand and Ansett Airlines are expected to take up United's offer to become part of the broader global grouping with Thai International Airways, Germany's Lufthansa Airways and Air Canada. Page 5.

Speaking about his appointment to the boards of three of Australia's largest industry superannuation funds, former Reserve Bank governor Bernie Fraser admitted there might be some bias against the funds and said he would try to redress the conception that they are run by the unions. Fraser will serve as an independent director for Superannuation Trust of Australia, Australian Retirement Fund and C+Bus. Page 19.

Australian gold producers are facing the worst conditions for selling gold since 1992, with the metal's price sliding from US$390 an ounce two months ago to just US$368 an ounce last night. The gold index dropped another 40.9 points yesterday as gold miners Placer Pacific, Normandy Ltd, Sons of Gwalia and Resolute were marked down. Page 19.

Highlands Gold Ltd yesterday labelled Placer Dome Inc's A$423 million takeover bid document as deficient and said Placer Dome failed to disclose its intentions or its full shareholding. However, Macquarie Corporate associate director Jim Craig said the takeover complies with Papua New Guinea law. Page 20.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The gold price will end the year close to US$350 an ounce, after the metal hit a three-year low yesterday. The slump prompted heavy selling of local gold stocks, with spot gold in Sydney ending at US$367.90 an ounce, down US$2.65. D&D Tolhurst commodity analyst Peter Graham said the gold market was under serious threat for the first time in two decades. Page 35.

Attending yesterday's opening session of the fourth National Trade and Investment Outlook Conference in Melbourne, Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer hinted that the Federal Government was likely to make a series of policy announcements early next year in response to business criticism about the lack of an overall industry policy framework. Fischer also reaffirmed the Government's commitment to trade liberalisation. Page 35.

In a move that will dramatically expand United Airlines' influence in Australasia, the US carrier yesterday announced a code sharing arrangement with Air New Zealand. However, United's Australian general manager, Anne Keating, said the airline had no intention of buying Qantas Airways Ltd's 19 per cent stake in Air New Zealand, claiming United gets as much influence through code sharing relationships as it does through equity stakes. Page 35.

Following a High Court ruling yesterday in the Spotless Services Ltd case, the Australian Taxation Office will have increased powers to attack offshore tax havens and other forms of tax avoidance. Overturning a ruling of the full Federal Court last year, the High Court ruled that Spotless made a A$40 million investment in the Cook Islands in 1987 for the dominant purpose of avoiding tax. Page 35.

Coming under criticism from shareholders for its low payout ratio over the past two years, George Weston Foods Ltd announced yesterday a A$94 million special payout on all ordinary shares. The fully franked special dividend of A$1 a share is in addition to a 17.5 cents a share total dividend payout of A$16.55 million for the financial year. Page 37.

Conrad Black's Hollinger International yesterday unveiled plans to sell US$800 million in debt securities or preferred stock and another US$500 million in debt or convertible securities in an effort to raise up to US$1.3 billion to reduce debt, redeem preference shares and for working capital, capital expenditure and acquisitions. Page 37.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The AMP Society will next week reveal its plan to demutualise, giving its two million policy holders a chance to participate in a A$12 billion-plus sharemarket listing in 1998. AMP will become the third big insurance group to transform from a mutual to alisted company in the past two years. Page 25.

The Australian Taxation Office scored a big win in the High Court yesterday, when the court ruled that Spotless Services group invested in the Cook Islands in the 1980s for the dominant purpose of obtaining a tax benefit. Some tax commentators believe the decision will give the ATO much broader powers to question tax-driven investment decisions, such as infrastructure bonds. Page 25.

Seeking to recover A$66.5 million paid in 1988 via the Bank of New Zealand to companies associated with disgraced New Zealand businessman Allan Hawkins, Foster's Brewing Group ended its legal battle yesterday without collecting a cent and agreeing to pay more than A$1 million for the legal costs of former directors John Elliott, Peter Scanlon and Ken Biggins, as well as the Bank of New Zealand and accountants Price Waterhouse. Page 25.

Industry commentators are concerned that Cinema Plus is struggling to meet prospectus forecasts, with the IMAX screen operator's shares dropping to 95 cents yesterday after listing at A$1.24. However, Cinema Plus is still expected to meet its 1996-97 net profit of A$2.7 million. Page 27.

The Federal Government's privatisation timetable for Telstra is set for a hiccup, with its huge package of legislation sure to be sent to a Senate legislative committee immediately after it is introduced into Parliament this week. The Democrats signalled last night they intend to take up the concerns of local government about overhead pay TV cabling and Telstra, Optus, resellers and potential new entrants are also expected to make further submissions. Page 27.

After stepping down from the Reserve Bank in September, former governor Bernie Fraser will become the trustee of the Superannuation Trust of Australia, the construction and building industry's C+Bus fund and the Australian Retirement Fund. As three of Australia's largest superannuation bodies, the funds hold more than A$3.7 billion in assets on behalf of about one million Australians. Page 27.
THE AGE

Delivering a blow to BHP, the president of South Korean steelmaker Posco, Kim Mahn-je, said in Melbourne yesterday that the company would look for alternative sources of raw materials because wage pressures and the high Australian dollar made it difficult for BHP to contain its costs. Page C1.

Foster's Brewing Group agreed to end its A$66.5 million lawsuit against former directors John Elliott, Peter Scanlon and Ken Biggins yesterday, in a move that sees it withdraw without a cent and paying out more than A$1 million for its opponents' legal cots. The agreement sees the end of a three-year battle for compensation over allegedly sham foreign exchange deals in the late 1980s. Page C1.

The Federal Government's new chief scientist yesterday questioned the Coalition's decision to cut tax breaks for research and development, claiming the surge in business spending on R&D since 1983 should be seen as a base on which Australia could build a strong R&D sector. Page C1.

Addressing a conference in Sydney yesterday, Singapore Airlines chief executive officer Cheong Choong Kong urged the Federal Government to deregulate the aviation market between Australia and South-East Asia to guarantee the future of the domestic tourism industry, claiming tourism growth from open-skies agreements with Asia could generate billions of dollars for the Australian economy. Page C3.

United Airlines and Air New Zealand have formed an alliance to strengthen their services to and from the South Pacific, which includes benefits such as an increase in the number of city-to-city connections between the two airlines, code-sharing arrangements between the US, New Zealand and Australia, mutual frequent-flier privileges and shared lounges. Page C3.

Former Reserve Bank governor Bernie Fraser will take up independent directorships on the boards of three of Australia's largest industry superannuation firms, Superannuation Trust of Australia, the Australian Retirement Fund and C+Bus, the fund for the costruction and building industries. Page C3.
